card: This PR optimizes legacy wallet migration to SQLite by skipping legacy wallet and transaction records during the initial copy rather than copying and subsequently erasing them. Because these records are either superseded by descriptor records or rewritten during migration, this omission simplifies the process and eliminates unused database record erasure methods (EraseTx, RemoveTxs, DeleteRecordsWithDB, EraseRecords). It addresses internal database churn during migration and cleans up dead wallet database code.
evidence: PR description: "When migrating a legacy wallet, we can skip the records in MigrateToSQLite that we would delete later on during migration... This allows us to remove several database record erase functions, specifically EraseTx and EraseRecords."
Commit messages and stats show net removal of 136 lines across 7 files, eliminating EraseTx, RemoveTxs, DeleteRecordsWithDB, and EraseRecords.
problem: Legacy wallet migration unnecessarily copies records into the destination SQLite database only to erase them moments later, adding redundant database operations and requiring maintenance of otherwise unused record deletion functions.

risk.why: A mistake in skipping records during database migration could result in missing wallet metadata or dropped transactions for users migrating legacy wallets.

scope_notes: Small refactor and dead-code cleanup across wallet database and migration files (+17/-153).
summary: Updates the legacy wallet migration to SQLite to skip writing legacy records and transaction records upfront instead of copying and then deleting them. Because these records are either replaced by descriptors or rewritten during migration, deleting them from the SQLite database is no longer needed. The change also removes several now-unused database record erasure functions and marks an internal legacy record check function static.
uncertainties: The patch diff was not provided, though the commit log and PR description describe the exact functions removed and modified.
